instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Lost in the Process
cards.instruction: Hide your role in the problem by distributing blame across steps, policies, and unnamed procedures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my slip in the tray like yours. Dispatch complete. Your parcel's stuck between reception and transport.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was scrap paper. You left the parcel on the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tray cleared. Dispatch handed it to transport without a receipt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both departments are you. Call the bus company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll report a failure across dispatch, transport and receipt control. They'll need to investigate all three.

beats.text: I've held my envelopes up to the light like you. Addresses verified. The birthday invitations failed somewhere in mailing.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You are the archive.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Outside the Scope
cards.instruction: Redirect personal or dangerous questions by declaring them irrelevant, premature, or assigned to another process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I raised my hand like you. Repairs only. Whether I broke the window is outside this meeting's scope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking how high the crack goes. Then let's hold a responsibility meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Height checked. After the repairs; we need a safe venue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can meet outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Location changes require a separate planning discussion.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've told the parents 'routine maintenance,' same as you. We mustn't make Mr Patel sound careless.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant the boiler. His bus is in the pond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, vehicle maintenance. Let's both say the trip is postponed while the bus is repaired.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's standing at the gate telling them he forgot the handbrake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll join him: 'Mr Patel is safe; the bus needs repairs.' Give him that sentence too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I clapped when you clapped. I've told everyone the gazebo fire was part of the entertainment; Grandad doesn't need complaints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was clapping for the magician. Grandad set fire to the gazebo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that part. From now on it's 'Everyone's fine; we're eating indoors.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Grandad's asking me whether he should apologize when he makes his speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to thank everyone for coming indoors. We'll use his words when anyone asks.

cards.title: For the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to state exactly what they did, knew, or authorized before you reveal your own involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've been telling the team 'cleared,' like you. Before I show you my order, what exactly did you clear?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The old stock from the storeroom. What did you order?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, clearing space. Did you authorize fireworks for the launch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Handheld sparklers. Nothing we'd have to light outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that wording in the email, then I'll forward the supplier's instructions.

beats.text: I've marked everyone's name 'plus one,' like you. Before we open my replies, who did you authorize to bring someone?

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Successful Compliance
cards.instruction: Describe a failed outcome as proof that the correct process was followed and therefore the system worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You made tipping that tray look so easy. I did the same with the cake stand; at least we followed the demonstration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was emptying crumbs into a bin. You tipped the wedding cake onto the floor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, different loads. Good thing we tested the stand before the guests arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've arrived. They're asking what we're serving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them we rejected the cake before serving it. Not one faulty slice reached a guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I marched everyone through the door you pointed at. We're all in the cupboard, so the drill kept us together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was pointing out where we keep the evacuation map.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. Everyone reached the map before choosing an exit. Nobody guessed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All twelve of us are packed against the door. I can't pull it open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can finish the headcount without losing anyone. Call that stage complete.
